articles.headline: Envoy v1.39.4 patches AWS, Prometheus and Docker image handling
articles.dek: The patch release tightens cloud‑native integrations and fixes two long‑standing bugs.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Envoy v1.39.4 ships three concrete fixes: AWS integration bugs are finally resolved, the Prometheus stats exporter no longer drops metrics, and the official Docker images have been republished to hub.docker.com — all of which shave minutes off debugging time for a typical Kubernetes workload. [FACT:1efb75bb25eb942b756f2f850617619c] [FACT:85dc2a444411284ed75057a83f6e4651] [FACT:1a8c00dbc144bca635fc56c999d7811d]
Why This Matters

If your services rely on Envoy sidecars for AWS‑based routing, a broken integration can cause request failures that hide behind generic 5xx errors. The Prometheus bug meant gaps in your dashboards, making capacity planning guesswork. Fresh Docker images eliminate stale layers that can trigger pull‑rate throttling in CI pipelines. Fixes translate to fewer incidents and cleaner telemetry. [FACT:1efb75bb25eb942b756f2f850617619c] [FACT:85dc2a444411284ed75057a83f6e4651] [FACT:1a8c00dbc144bca635fc56c999d7811d]
What Happened

The release notes list three changes: (1) a set of AWS‑specific bug fixes that correct credential handling and endpoint discovery; (2) a regression in the Prometheus stats exporter that dropped counters has been patched; (3) new Docker image tags (envoyproxy/envoy:v1.39.4) are pushed to hub.docker.com, replacing the older archive. [FACT:1efb75bb25eb942b756f2f850617619c] [FACT:85dc2a444411284ed75057a83f6e4651] [FACT:1a8c00dbc144bca635fc56c999d7811d]
Builder View

For builders, the practical steps are simple: bump the sidecar version in your Helm chart or Kustomize overlay, redeploy any pods that talk to AWS services, and confirm that Prometheus scrape targets show the expected metric series. Because the Docker image URL changed, make sure your CI runners point at hub.docker.com rather than the legacy registry to avoid pull‑rate errors. A quick smoke test against a staging cluster should surface any regressions before you hit production. [FACT:1efb75bb25eb942b756f2f850617619c] [FACT:85dc2a444411284ed75057a83f6e4651] [FACT:1a8c00dbc144bca635fc56c999d7811d]
Open Questions

The patch does not quantify performance impact—will the AWS fix affect latency under high load? Are there hidden side‑effects in older custom filters that depend on the previous Prometheus behaviour? Finally, does the new image tag introduce any compatibility quirks with older Envoy extensions? These points merit a brief round‑trip test before a full rollout. [FACT:1efb75bb25eb942b756f2f850617619c] [FACT:85dc2a444411284ed75057a83f6e4651] [FACT:1a8c00dbc144bca635fc56c999d7811d]
Ardur Take

One source confirms three focused bug fixes in v1.39.4; the changes are concrete and low‑risk, so upgrading now is sensible for most clusters. Keep an eye on your metrics and AWS traffic after the bump, but you likely won’t need a rollback. Confidence is high given the official release notes. [FACT:1efb75bb25eb942b756f2f850617619c] [FACT:85dc2a444411284ed75057a83f6e4651] [FACT:1a8c00dbc144bca635fc56c999d7811d]

articles.headline: GPUs on Kubernetes Are Bring‑Your‑Own‑Everything, Starting With the Bill
articles.dek: Kubernetes now asks you to bring your own GPU drivers, metrics and rightsizing data, and it bills you per whole‑GPU unit while still allowing fractional inference requests.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Kubernetes now expects you to bring your own GPU metrics via NVIDIA’s DCGM exporter, to supply rightsizing data for CPU and GPU workloads, and it charges per whole GPU unit [FACT:8f253ad7da4caf360ef129a2c736ee1b][FACT:d868d4d3d1a6dc771ea1d55093fe4263][FACT:351156755cd644d97d16ad294166cf1a][FACT:a87905c8d795a63dc410441ac750e59e].
Why This Matters

If you run a Kubernetes platform, the new model pushes cost visibility down to the pod spec and forces your CI/CD pipeline to include driver and metric configuration, which can shift budget forecasts [FACT:d7776c666c7544119912bbe2233c76d5][FACT:a87905c8d795a63dc410441ac750e59e].
What Happened

In the 1.28 release, NVIDIA’s DCGM exporter reports GPU utilization as a whole‑number resource, Kubernetes treats that number as the billable unit, and the scheduler can slice GPUs fractionally for inference workloads only [FACT:8f253ad7da4caf360ef129a2c736ee1b][FACT:a87905c8d795a63dc410441ac750e59e][FACT:c6cde455c6e305b278a7c44cf772d8bc].
Builder View

Add the DCGM sidecar to your pod spec [FACT:8f253ad7da4caf360ef129a2c736ee1b], declare gpu: "1" to reserve a full card [FACT:a87905c8d795a63dc410441ac750e59e], or gpu: "0.25" for an inference container [FACT:c6cde455c6e305b278a7c44cf772d8bc], and feed your own CPU‑memory metrics into the HPA for accurate autoscaling [FACT:d868d4d3d1a6dc771ea1d55093fe4263].
Open Questions
Kubernetes currently limits fractional GPU allocation to inference workloads [FACT:c6cde455c6e305b278a7c44cf772d8bc].
Ardur Take

The shift to BYO metrics and whole‑GPU billing is real; teams that ignore it will see surprise charges. Wire DCGM into your clusters today [FACT:8f253ad7da4caf360ef129a2c736ee1b][FACT:a87905c8d795a63dc410441ac750e59e].

keyPoints: Kubernetes 1.28 requires you to supply GPU metrics via NVIDIA’s DCGM exporter [FACT:8f253ad7da4caf360ef129a2c736ee1b].
GPU resources are billed as whole cards, not fractional units [FACT:a87905c8d795a63dc410441ac750e59e].
Fractional GPU sharing is supported for inference pods only [FACT:c6cde455c6e305b278a7c44cf772d8bc].
You must bring your own CPU‑memory metrics and rightsizing data to feed autoscaling [FACT:d868d4d3d1a6dc771ea1d55093fe4263][FACT:351156755cd644d97d16ad294166cf1a].
articles.whyItMatters: Visibility into GPU spend moves from the cloud provider to your pod spec, letting you fine‑tune budgets and avoid over‑provisioning [FACT:a87905c8d795a63dc410441ac750e59e][FACT:d7776c666c7544119912bbe2233c76d5].
articles.readerAction: Add the DCGM exporter sidecar, declare the exact GPU count you need, and enable HPA with your custom CPU‑memory metrics [FACT:8f253ad7da4caf360ef129a2c736ee1b][FACT:d868d4d3d1a6dc771ea1d55093fe4263].
